title: Night over Chajnantor
caption: The night sky over ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: This 360 degree panorama shows the night sky over the Chajnantor plateau, with the antennas of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, ALMA, standing all around. The photograph is by Petr Horálek.

A full-circle panorama wraps the entire horizon into a single image, so the sky and the landscape can appear curved or stretched compared with an ordinary photo. It is a way of capturing what it would feel like to stand in the middle of the array and turn slowly around.

ALMA observes the sky at millimetre and submillimetre wavelengths, light far beyond the colours our eyes can detect. Rather than a single mirror, it uses many dish antennas working together. Those antennas share the frame with a sky full of stars that ordinary visible light reveals.

understand.summary: This is a 360 degree panorama taken in visible light with a camera at ALMA. The camera settings, colour processing and projection are not published.
understand.eye: No eye can take in a full circle at once. The panorama stitches the whole horizon into one frame, and the long exposures show more stars than a person would see.

explore: ESO also offers virtual tours of its sites, which let visitors explore places like the Chajnantor plateau from afar. This panorama gives a similar feel of standing among ALMA's antennas at night.
alt: A 360 degree panorama of a starry night sky above the antennas of ALMA on a high plateau.
